title: Is Tooth Extraction Painful? Pain, Recovery & What to Eat
seoTitle: Is Tooth Extraction Painful? Recovery and Diet
seoDescription: Pain after an extraction usually peaks within 48 hours and eases over days. Get a day-by-day eating plan and warning signs from our Valencia team.
excerpt: How much an extraction hurts, how long it lasts, a phase-by-phase eating plan to protect the clot, and the signs that mean you should call.
keyTakeaways: Local anesthesia means little or no pain during the procedure; afterward pain usually peaks in the first 24 to 48 hours.
Simple extractions settle in 3 to 7 days; surgical or impacted wisdom tooth removals can take two weeks or longer.
Avoid straws for 7 to 10 days, spoon smoothies and soups, keep food cool to lukewarm, and chew on the opposite side.
Start with yogurt, broth and mashed foods, add soft solids on days 3 to 7, and return to regular textures after 1 to 2 weeks.
Call if pain increases after 72 hours, bleeding soaks gauze every 30 to 60 minutes, or you have fever or foul drainage.

flags: Heading says avoid certain foods for the 'first 2–8 weeks' and the body says 'at least four weeks after surgical extractions'; the 8-week figure is inconsistent with the rest of the article and looks excessive.
Relies on Reddit anecdotes ('One redditor...', recurrent swelling after two antibiotic courses) that are unverifiable.
Citations to AAOMS, Mayo Clinic, NHS and ADA are homepage links, except the NHS dental abscess page.
